# Create dataset with 42 countries, and view variant dynamic plots {.tabset}

(Adapted from Nathan's global wave metrics workbook)

Final data point selected as the first epi week in which >10% of cases were the variant we are trying to predict (see name printed below, cases as inferred from GISAID sequence proportions). 42 countries are included: countries that have greater than 10 sequences per week between June 01 2021 to June 01 2022, minus India and Singapore who did not have workable Delta/BA.1/BA.2 periods. 


```{r, Plots-Delineated, results = "asis"}
# Customize to specific dataset you want to create:

# List of countries:
cs <- read_csv("../../data/42_countries.csv")
my_regions <- cs$Country

# Start and end dates for plotting:
mindate <- "2021-03-01"
maxepidate <- "2022-04-01"

# Variant to generate for predicting
var <- "Omicron BA.1*"
# e.g.  "Alpha*"           "Beta"             "Delta*"           "Epsilon"          "Gamma"            "Iota"         
# "Kappa"            "Lambda"           "Mu"               "Omicron BA.1*"    "Omicron BA.2*"    "Omicron BA.2.75*"
# "Omicron BA.4*"    "Omicron BA.5*"    "Omicron BQ.*"     "Recombinants"     "XBB*"             "other"           
# "wildtype A*"      "wildtype B*"  

# File to output to
outfile <- "../../data/Dates_42countriesDeltaBA1.csv"

print(paste0("Generating dates for predicting ", var, ", compared to previous variant"))

```

```{r}
# Generate the end dates
dates <- tibble(country = my_regions, end_date = rep(NA, length(my_regions)), wk4 = rep(NA, length(my_regions)) , wk3 = rep(NA, length(my_regions)), wk2 = rep(NA, length(my_regions)), wk1 = rep(NA,length(my_regions)))

for (location in my_regions) {
  # Subset data by region
  region_owid <- owid_data_w[owid_data_w$location == location, ]
  region_gisaid <- gisaid_data_w[gisaid_data_w$location == location, ]

  # Creating peaks
  cases <- region_owid$weekly_cases
  cases[is.na(cases)] <- 0
  cases[is.nan(cases)] <- 0

  peaks <- find_peaks(cases, tolerance = 4)
  valleys <- find_valleys(cases, peaks)

  # aesthetics
  noepiweeks <- 6 # number of epi weeks in proportions plot
  ticks <- "1 month" # 2 months = cadence of ticks (by month)

  # - variant data
  region_gisaid %>%
    dplyr::select(week, VOC, proportion) %>%
    filter(week > mindate) %>% filter(week < maxepidate) %>% # cut sequences found before 1st date of weekly_cases
    filter(!is.na(week)) -> dfin # remove weeks with NAs
  as.data.frame(dfin) -> dfprop # flatten

  dfprop %>% complete(week, VOC, fill = list(proportion = 0)) -> dfprop2 # fill in missing weeks with zero values

  dfprop2 %>%
    group_by(week, VOC) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(across(everything(), sum), .groups = "keep") -> dfprop3 
  # sum props and mult of same VOC
  # note, had to include ".groups = keep" to suppress grouping message from knit.

  merge(dfprop3, region_owid, all.x = T) -> dfplot # merge dfs

  dfplot$mult <- dfplot$weekly_cases * as.numeric(dfplot$proportion) # n*proportion  -> for plotting
  
  # Find date of first week for which BA.2 prop is >0.1
  endd <- dfplot %>% filter(VOC==var) %>% filter(proportion > 0.1) %>% 
    summarize(First = min(week))
  # Generate the successive weeks backward
  dates[dates$country==location,2] <- endd$First
  dates[dates$country==location,3] <- endd$First - 7
  dates[dates$country==location,4] <- endd$First - 14
  dates[dates$country==location,5] <- endd$First - 21
  dates[dates$country==location,6] <- endd$First - 28
  
}

print("Creating end dates table and saving to file...")



# Save the CSV
write_csv(dates, outfile)

```


Lastly we plot those dates on top of the variant case curves. 

* Waves as identified by Nathan's script are bounded by red lines
* Red dots identify wave peaks.
* Black lines indicate the final data point included in the data set for prediction. We also include 4 earlier data points, taken 1 week incrementally backwards from the black line.
* White space indicates there is no sequencing data for that time


```{r}

plots1 <- list() # create empty list to store plots


for (location in my_regions) {
  # Subset data by region
  region_owid <- owid_data_w[owid_data_w$location == location, ]
  region_gisaid <- gisaid_data_w[gisaid_data_w$location == location, ]


  # Creating peaks
  cases <- region_owid$weekly_cases

  cases[is.na(cases)] <- 0
  cases[is.nan(cases)] <- 0

  peaks <- find_peaks(cases, tolerance = 4)

  valleys <- find_valleys(cases, peaks)


  # - variant data

  region_gisaid %>%
    dplyr::select(week, VOC, proportion) %>%
    filter(week > mindate) %>% filter(week < maxepidate) %>%
    filter(!is.na(week)) -> dfin 
  as.data.frame(dfin) -> dfprop 

  dfprop %>% complete(week, VOC, fill = list(proportion = 0)) -> dfprop2

  dfprop2 %>%
    group_by(week, VOC) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(across(everything(), sum), .groups = "keep") -> dfprop3 

  merge(dfprop3, region_owid, all.x = T) -> dfplot # merge dfs

  dfplot$mult <- dfplot$weekly_cases * as.numeric(dfplot$proportion) # n*proportion  -> for plotting

  # Plotting:
  # Large VD plot
  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_area(data = dfplot, aes(x = as.Date(week), y = mult, fill = VOC)) +
    geom_line(data = region_owid, aes(x = as.Date(week), y = weekly_cases), size = 0.75) + 
    xlim(as.Date(mindate), as.Date(maxepidate)) +
    scale_fill_manual(breaks = names(pal), values = pal) +
    geom_point(data = region_owid[peaks, ], aes(x = week, y = weekly_cases), color = "red") +
    geom_vline(data = region_owid[valleys, ], aes(xintercept = week), color = "red", alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = dates[dates$country==location,2]$end_date, lwd=1) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = dates[dates$country==location,3]$wk4, lwd=0.5) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = dates[dates$country==location,4]$wk3, lwd=0.5) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = dates[dates$country==location,5]$wk2, lwd=0.5) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = dates[dates$country==location,6]$wk1, lwd=0.5) +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = "weekly case counts",
      title = location,
      # subtitle = "subtitle", #add a subtitle here if wanted
      caption = "Notes: Weekly case counts and lineage proportions. Data sources: OWID, GISAID"
    ) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      plot.caption = element_text(size = 6, hjust = 0, face = "italic"),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.caption.position = "plot",
      legend.title = element_blank(),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 17, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(name = "Cases", labels = comma) 

  plots1[[location]] <- p # save each new plot to the index of location in the plots list
}



pl_list <- list() # create empty list to store plots and labels
for (location in my_regions) {
  pl_list[[location]] <- list(plots1[[location]], location) # create new list with each element containing a plot and a title to print in tabs
}

# note, this only works with chunk option set with results = "asis"
for (location in my_regions) {
  tmp <- pl_list[[location]]
  #catHeader(tmp[[2]], 2) # this uses the second item in tmp as the title, and uses the second header level
  lapply(tmp[1], print) # this prints the first item in tmp
}
```
